title: Square-zero coordinates on a local ring with a residue section
statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with maximal ideal m and residue field K. Suppose s:K -> A is a ring map whose composite with reduction is the identity. Put d=m.spanFinrank. There exists a ring isomorphism e:A/m^2 -> K plus K^d, the trivial square-zero extension [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], such that the first coordinate of e(a mod m^2) is the residue of a for every a in A.

source.place: Tag 07EI, construction of f_1; coefficient field from Algebra Tag 032A

proof.text: Nakayama identifies the dimension of V=m/m^2 over K with d=m.spanFinrank. Choose a basis indexed by Fin d, giving a linear equivalence V = K^d. In Lean use IsLocalRing.spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace and Module.finBasisOfFinrankEq.

The section s defines a K-algebra structure on A and A/m^2. The canonical injection j:V -> A/m^2 is K-linear: the action of s(c) on V equals multiplication by its residue c. The image of j has square zero, since products of elements of m vanish modulo m^2.

Use the universal lift of the trivial square-zero extension to define F(c,v)=s(c)+j(v), using the chosen coordinates. Reduction of F(c,v) is c. If F(c,v)=F(c_prime,v_prime), reduction gives c=c_prime, and injectivity of j gives v=v_prime.

For any a in A, a-s(residue(a)) lies in m. Its cotangent class supplies v such that F(residue(a),v)=a modulo m^2, so F is surjective. Invert this bijective ring map. The first coordinate of the inverse is reduction, as required.

theorem exists_firstOrder_coordinates (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (s : ResidueField A →+* A)
    (hs : (residue A).comp s = RingHom.id _) :
    ∃ e : (A ⧸ maximalIdeal A ^ 2) ≃+*
        TrivSqZeroExt (ResidueField A) (Fin (maximalIdeal A).spanFinrank → ResidueField A),
      ∀ a : A, (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal A ^ 2) a)).fst = residue A a
